turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. The pharmacy technician has left me your repeat list. This is that review, and you've asked for something stronger for the pain?
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right knee worse since when?
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Since Diwali, or after it. You can't pin it down?
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): I won't invent a date, then. Is the pain there most days?
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it wake you at night?
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any swelling in the knee?
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does the knee give way?
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is the knee stiff in the morning?
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Heartburn, or pain in the stomach?
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Quick look. Crepitus on bending the right knee, no effusion, and it's tender along the medial joint line.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry. Notes say osteoarthritis of that knee, for years.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any operation on it, ever?

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Retired. Filthy weather, isn't it, the bus was late. Anyway, paracetamol one gram, two five-hundred milligram tablets, four times a day, for the knee. That the dose you use?
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): And do you actually take all four doses?
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Prescribed four times a day, then, but I can't say you stick to it. Does the naproxen ease the knee?
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's a suppose. I won't record it as helping. What strength are you on?
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Naproxen for the knee: you say two hundred and fifty milligrams twice a day, and the pharmacy list says five hundred milligrams twice a day. They don't agree.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): I won't guess which is right. When did you start the naproxen?
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Last winter. Or the one before.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Last winter, or the one before. No date on that either. Omeprazole, ten— no, twenty milligrams each morning, for the stomach. Still on it?
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Amlodipine I nearly called ten milligrams. It's five milligrams once a day, for the blood pressure. Yes?
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any other tablets at home?
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): The stronger painkiller, what did you want?
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): I keep turning over a flare, ordinary wear, or a bit of cartilage catching, and I am not going to conclude any of those today.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): No tramadol, and no codeine. They'll doze you and bung you up, and they won't fix a worn knee. I'm declining both.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): From what you've told me and from the examination, my working impression is only this: the osteoarthritis is grumbling more, not a fresh injury.
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll reissue the paracetamol, the omeprazole and the amlodipine. I'm holding the naproxen repeat until the strength is sorted. Bring the box next time.
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): Take the paracetamol more regularly if you can, not just odd doses. No extra anti-inflammatory on top.
[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): I might send you for an x-ray of the right knee if it's no better in three months. Not booking it now.
[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll see you back here in three months. If the pain gets worse before that, come back sooner.

[SEG0069] person_1 (DOCTOR): Saying it back: right knee pain worse since Diwali or after, most days, set off by walking and stairs, and it wakes you at night. Paracetamol one gram four times a day on the script, not reliably taken. Naproxen dose still disputed, two-fifty against five hundred, both twice daily. Omeprazole twenty each morning, amlodipine five once a day. No stronger painkiller. Anything twisted?
[SEG0071] person_1 (DOCTOR): And you still can't put a time on the Diwali business, or on when the naproxen started?

spec.situation: Routine repeat-prescription review at a small clinic with a pharmacy technician present; patient wants a stronger painkiller; tablet names and doses are discussed in detail, one dose is read from the pharmacy list and differs from the patient's own; doctor declines the stronger medicine.
features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
